concerns.location: tasks.md:Compute feasibility note + T004/T006/T007/T009 vs spec.md:FR-008, SC-009
concerns.text: Tasks mandate real GPU (Kaggle CUDA) verifier inference, but FR-008 requires all analysis steps to complete 'within a 6-hour runtime on a CPU-only runner with ≤ 7 GB RAM' and SC-009 requires baseline runtime '≤ 2 hours on a CPU-only runner'. T006 asserts SC-009 while running on GPU — the criterion as specified is unmeasurable under the tasked workflow. Either amend the spec/SC-009 to authorize GPU offload or task a CPU-executable measurement; silently reinterpreting 'CPU-only runner' as 'Kaggle GPU' is a semantic weakening of a MUST-level constraint.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Compute feasibility note vs constitution.md:Principle I
concerns.text: Constitution Principle I (NON-NEGOTIABLE) requires every result reproducible 'on a fresh GitHub Actions runner'. Tasks route all verifier inference to a free Kaggle GPU with execution-stage auto-offload, so reported results cannot be reproduced on the constitutionally mandated runner. This is silent constitution drift introduced by the task list; needs explicit reconciliation (amendment or documented CPU path).

Spec assumes the public repository 'contains sufficient examples of multi-step conflicting instructions' to curate the dataset, but T002 constructs the 500 conflicting prompts by synthetically composing/injecting contradictions into neutral prompts. This is a material change in dataset provenance the spec never authorizes; the spec must be amended to document the synthetic-conflict construction or the tasks must curate real conflicting examples.

T008 runs hypothesis tests on the neutral subset and both control conditions (filler/empty) with BH correction 'across all hypothesis tests', but the report schema's tests object and multiple_comparison_correction.adjusted_p_values only accommodate 'primary' and 'robustness' keys. The neutral/control test results have no representable home in the contract-conformant report.json — either the schema must be extended or T008's deliverable silently drops required test results.

SC-007 (Pearson r ≥ 0.5) and SC-008 (Cohen's d ≥ 0.5) are pass/fail success criteria, but T008 only computes/reports them and T010's validation checks (a)–(d) include no assertion against these thresholds. The acceptance criteria are silently narrowed from 'must meet' to 'must report'.

T002 requires human_validation.csv to contain an n_raters column (check: n_raters ≥ 3), but the data model defines only prompt_id, human_rating, annotation_source. Update the data model so the check is verifiable against the declared contract.

T003 imposes the plan's graph-abstraction constraint ('principle identifiers only — no paraphrased clauses') but the data-model schema defines node label as 'principle text' with no abstraction requirement. The schema and the tasked parser output disagree; align the data model with the plan constraint.

SC-005's robustness criterion is an effect-size-difference test (no significant drop, p ≥ 0.05), but the schema's test_result only permits paired_t_test/wilcoxon with a single effect size, which does not represent an effect-size comparison. T009 promises the result 'in report.json as tests.robustness' — the schema cannot express it as specified; reconcile schema or criterion.
